groups.title: Thinking & interpretation
groups.description: How we form explanations, check beliefs and judge other people.

entries.title: Confirmation bias
entries.summary: Why we favour evidence that fits a belief, how to notice it, and how to check fairly.
entries.keywords: beliefs evidence assumptions selective attention motivated reasoning

entries.title: Correspondence bias
entries.summary: Why we explain behaviour through character and overlook the situation.
entries.keywords: attribution personality character situation fundamental attribution error

entries.title: Identity & beliefs
entries.summary: A belief can connect to someone’s experience, commitments and sense of who they are.

entries.title: Observation & interpretation
entries.summary: Separate what someone said or did from your explanation of it.

entries.title: Truth, lies & uncertainty
entries.summary: Check claims through relevant evidence. Eye contact, nervousness, confidence or a compelling story do not reliably establish honesty.

entries.title: Uncertainty
entries.summary: Not knowing what is happening or what will happen next can be relevant to an interaction.

entries.title: Assumptions in questions & decision rights
entries.summary: Separate what a question asks from what it assumes, and a proposal from a decision someone is entitled to make.
entries.keywords: loaded questions presupposition implicature framing epistemic deontic authority agenda control who decides patronising

entries.title: Compare occasions & test an explanation
entries.summary: Investigate recurrence, exceptions and competing explanations through proportionate observation, action and review.
entries.keywords: one off repeated pattern compare occasions hypothesis diary journal observation evidence exceptions causality intention conditioning strategy

groups.title: Behaviour & relationships
groups.description: Recognise actions and patterns, compare possible explanations and examine your own contribution.

entries.title: Declining help
entries.summary: Compare reasons for turning down help, change the offer and review what happens.
entries.keywords: refusing help independence autonomy competence family support

entries.title: Acknowledging another perspective
entries.summary: Recognising the concern or experience someone expresses without claiming you agree with every conclusion.

entries.title: Agreeing, then not following through
entries.summary: Someone agrees to an action, but it does not happen as expected.

entries.title: Avoiding vulnerability
entries.summary: Holding back feelings, uncertainty or needs that would expose something personally important.
entries.keywords: i cannot open up they never share feelings afraid to be vulnerable avoid vulnerability

entries.title: Contempt & belittling
entries.summary: Communicating that another person is inferior or not worth taking seriously, for example through ridicule or degrading remarks.
entries.keywords: they mock me they talk down to me they humiliate me contempt

entries.title: Control of money & resources
entries.summary: Restricting access to money, information, work or essentials in a way that limits another person’s choices.
entries.keywords: they control all the money they take my wages financial abuse i have to ask for money

entries.title: Deflecting or changing the subject
entries.summary: Moving a discussion away from the issue being raised, so it remains unresolved.
entries.keywords: whataboutism they change the subject what about when you they avoid answering

entries.title: Denying an event or agreement
entries.summary: Rejecting an account of what was said, done or agreed. The denial itself does not establish whether the person is mistaken or being deceptive.
entries.keywords: they deny it happened they never said that they deny saying things denying promises

entries.title: Difficulty trusting
entries.summary: Finding it hard to rely on another person’s word, intentions or handling of something important.
entries.keywords: i cannot trust anyone i dont trust them difficulty trusting they distrust everyone

entries.title: Dismissing another person’s needs
entries.summary: Responding to a stated need or feeling as though it does not deserve consideration. This describes a response, not a measurement of someone’s capacity for empathy.
entries.keywords: they dont care about my needs no empathy they ignore my feelings lack of empathy

entries.title: Emotional blackmail & conditional threats
entries.summary: An everyday term for pressure that makes avoiding a threatened emotional or relational consequence conditional on compliance.
entries.keywords: emotional blackmail if you leave ill do this or i will they threaten consequences unless i agree

entries.title: Entitlement, admiration & others’ needs
entries.summary: Behaviours often described as narcissistic include demanding special treatment, seeking admiration or repeatedly discounting others’ needs. These descriptions do not establish narcissistic personality disorder.
entries.keywords: narcissist narcissism narcissistic is this narcissistic they think they are special is this person a narcissist

entries.title: Favours that create unwanted obligation
entries.summary: Giving help or gifts that are later treated as creating obligations the recipient did not agree to.
entries.keywords: strings attached they hold favours over me i owe them unwanted gifts

entries.title: Gaslighting & undermining your reality
entries.summary: A pattern of undermining someone’s confidence in their memory, perception or account of events, often through denial, distortion or attacks on their credibility.
entries.keywords: gas lighting they deny saying things they tell me i imagined it you are imagining things they say im crazy they make me doubt my memory my partner says I imagined it says I imagined things says it never happened

entries.title: Guilt-tripping & pressure through obligation
entries.summary: Using guilt or a claimed duty to press someone toward a choice, especially when their refusal is not accepted.
entries.keywords: guilt trip after all ive done for you if you cared you would they make me feel guilty

entries.title: Indirect resistance & passive aggression
entries.summary: An everyday description of opposition or resentment expressed indirectly rather than through a clear disagreement.
entries.keywords: passive aggressive they agree but sabotage sarcastic digs they express anger indirectly

entries.title: Interrupting
entries.summary: Beginning to speak before another person has finished.

entries.title: Intimidation & threats
entries.summary: Words or actions that create fear of consequences, such as threats, menacing conduct or destruction of belongings.
entries.keywords: they threaten me i feel scared to say no they smash things intimidating

entries.title: Involving a third person
entries.summary: Bringing another person into a disagreement, whether for help, mediation or influence.

entries.title: Listening and checking understanding
entries.summary: Giving someone room to speak, then checking whether you understood what matters to them.

entries.title: Minimising harm or impact
entries.summary: Treating an effect on someone as too small or unreasonable to deserve attention.
entries.keywords: youre too sensitive it was just a joke you are overreacting they say it was nothing minimizing

entries.title: Monitoring & demands for access
entries.summary: Checking messages, movements or accounts, or demanding access to them. Consent and the ability to withdraw it matter.
entries.keywords: they check my phone they track my location they demand my passwords surveillance

entries.title: People-pleasing & automatic agreement
entries.summary: Agreeing or accommodating before checking one’s own wishes, limits or capacity, often to avoid disappointing someone.
entries.keywords: people pleasing i always say yes i cant say no i put everyone else first

entries.title: Possessiveness & demands for exclusivity
entries.summary: Treating another person’s attention, time or relationships as something one is entitled to control.
entries.keywords: possessive they act like they own me they demand all my time not allowed other friends

entries.title: Repair after a misunderstanding
entries.summary: Returning to an exchange to clarify, take responsibility for your actions and discuss what could work differently.

entries.title: Repeated criticism
entries.summary: Repeated negative comments about someone’s actions, choices or work. Describe the comments before interpreting the pattern.

entries.title: Repeatedly asking for reassurance
entries.summary: Returning to a question or request for reassurance after receiving an answer.

entries.title: Repeatedly pushing a stated limit
entries.summary: Continuing to press, bypass or test a limit after it has been communicated.
entries.keywords: they wont take no they keep asking after i say no ignore my boundaries boundary pushing

entries.title: Responding defensively
entries.summary: Pushing back against perceived criticism, for example by justifying, denying or counter-criticising.

entries.title: Restricting contact with other people
entries.summary: Interfering with someone’s access to friends, family, work or other support.
entries.keywords: they stop me seeing friends they isolate me i cannot see my family cut off from friends

entries.title: Restriction, monitoring & coercive patterns
entries.summary: Repeated restrictions, threats, monitoring or control of money and contact can limit someone’s freedom. The impact matters even when intent is disputed.

entries.title: Retaliation after a refusal or complaint
entries.summary: An adverse action following a refusal, disagreement or complaint that may be intended to impose a cost.
entries.keywords: they punish me for saying no revenge after a complaint they retaliate punished for disagreeing

entries.title: Shifting responsibility
entries.summary: Moving responsibility for an action onto someone else instead of addressing the part the speaker chose or controlled.
entries.keywords: blame shifting everything is my fault they blame me for their actions you made me do it

entries.title: Stonewalling, silence & an agreed pause
entries.summary: A term used for shutting down or refusing engagement in a discussion. Distinguish an indefinite refusal from a pause or a decision not to engage.
entries.keywords: silent treatment stonewalling they shut me out they refuse to discuss anything

entries.title: Taking or withholding credit
entries.summary: Claiming a contribution one did not make, or leaving another person’s contribution unrecognised.
entries.keywords: they take credit for my work they steal my ideas no credit taking credit

entries.title: Taking too much responsibility
entries.summary: Taking on responsibility for outcomes or other people’s reactions beyond what one can reasonably control or has agreed to do.
entries.keywords: everything is my responsibility i have to fix everyone over responsibility i feel responsible for their feelings

entries.title: Withdrawing from a conversation
entries.summary: Someone reduces contact or stops taking part in a conversation.

entries.title: Names, respect & belonging
entries.summary: How names and titles can express familiarity, belonging or rank, and what a naming difference does not establish.
entries.keywords: naming asymmetry names titles honorifics kinship matriarch patriarch mother in law inlaws face saving respect insiders outsiders

entries.title: Different standards & unequal treatment
entries.summary: Compare favouritism and double standards with differences that reflect needs, responsibilities or prior agreements.
entries.keywords: favouritism favoritism double standards differential treatment siblings golden child scapegoat unfair rules inlaws comparisons

entries.title: Pressure, withdrawal & interaction cycles
entries.summary: Understand repeated sequences in which each person’s response changes what happens next.
entries.keywords: demand withdraw pursue withdraw escalation cycle stonewalling silent treatment argument reassurance co regulation

entries.title: Escalating requests & everyday influence
entries.summary: Recognise request sequences, reconsider each decision and distinguish persuasion from pressure.

entries.title: Exclusion, gossip & reputation
entries.summary: Distinguish being excluded from restriction of your contacts, and check how stories about people are transmitted.
entries.keywords: ostracism exclusion gossip reputation rumours rumors smear campaign social proof shunning ignoring triangulation third party

entries.title: Denial, attack & blame reversal
entries.summary: Recognise a sequence that redirects accountability while distinguishing it from legitimate defence or counter-complaint.

entries.title: Changing criteria & moving goalposts
entries.summary: Distinguish justified revisions from repeated changes that make an agreement impossible to satisfy.

entries.title: Intense affection & inconsistent contact
entries.summary: Examine pace, consent, reliability and impact behind labels such as love bombing or breadcrumbing.

groups.title: Needs, goals & intentions
groups.description: What matters to people, competing priorities and the limits of inferring intentions.

entries.title: Belonging
entries.summary: Wanting connection, acceptance or a place in a group.

entries.title: Capability, opportunity & motivation
entries.summary: Explore whether a change needs knowledge or skill, different circumstances, or attention to competing motives and habits.

entries.title: Competing goals
entries.summary: Two desired outcomes can call for different actions at the same time.

entries.title: Fair treatment
entries.summary: Wanting an arrangement or process that feels fair. People can disagree about what fairness requires.

entries.title: Feeling capable
entries.summary: Wanting to be effective and able to meet a challenge.

entries.title: Feeling safe
entries.summary: Wanting safety, predictability or protection from a feared loss.

entries.title: Having a say
entries.summary: Wanting meaningful choice or ownership over what you do.

entries.title: Motivation
entries.summary: Explore what someone wants, what competes with it and what makes action possible.

entries.title: Recognition & status
entries.summary: Wanting respect, recognition or influence in a group.

entries.title: Seeking approval
entries.summary: Giving substantial weight to others’ favourable reactions when making choices or judging one’s own worth.
entries.keywords: i need everyone to like me approval seeking i need praise they need constant approval

entries.title: Trying to avoid conflict
entries.summary: A possible intention to prevent an argument or its consequences.

entries.title: Trying to persuade
entries.summary: A possible intention to change someone’s view or decision. It must be examined in the particular situation.

entries.title: Trying to protect
entries.summary: A possible intention to prevent harm or loss to someone.

entries.title: Trying to punish
entries.summary: A possible intention to impose a cost in response to a perceived wrong. This is a substantial claim about purpose.

entries.title: Trying to retain a role
entries.summary: A possible intention to preserve a familiar role or involvement in decisions.

groups.title: Personality & individual differences
groups.description: Understand broad traits, variation across situations and the limits of labels.

entries.title: Agreeableness
entries.summary: A broad personality dimension involving tendencies such as cooperation and consideration.

entries.title: Conscientiousness
entries.summary: A broad personality dimension including tendencies toward organisation and dependability.

entries.title: Extraversion
entries.summary: A broad personality dimension related to tendencies such as sociability and assertiveness.

entries.title: Negative emotionality
entries.summary: A broad personality dimension involving tendencies to experience distress, worry or emotional volatility. It is also often called neuroticism.

entries.title: Open-mindedness / openness
entries.summary: A broad personality dimension involving tendencies such as intellectual curiosity, imagination and aesthetic sensitivity.

entries.title: Personality facets & situation differences
entries.summary: Use narrower trait distinctions while avoiding character judgments from a few incidents.
entries.keywords: facets personality nuances assertiveness sociability organisation organization productivity compassion respectfulness trust big five traits

groups.title: Emotion, habits & learning
groups.description: Stress, expectations and patterns that can develop or change over time.

entries.title: Consequences that sustain a pattern
entries.summary: Consider whether what follows a behaviour makes its repetition worthwhile or relieves a difficulty.

entries.title: Fear of rejection
entries.summary: Concern about being unwanted, excluded or left. It can shape how ambiguous interactions are interpreted.
entries.keywords: fear of abandonment they will leave me afraid of rejection rejection sensitive

entries.title: Habits & situations
entries.summary: Repeated responses may be tied to familiar cues and circumstances.

entries.title: Jealousy & what follows
entries.summary: Concern about losing a valued relationship or position. The feeling and the actions taken in response need separate consideration.
entries.keywords: jealous they get jealous fear of losing someone jealousy

entries.title: Learned expectations
entries.summary: Past experience can shape what a person expects from an interaction. Do not invent that history from present behaviour.

entries.title: Perfectionism & inflexible standards
entries.summary: Holding standards so tightly that errors, stopping or accepting an adequate result become difficult.
entries.keywords: nothing is ever good enough perfectionist i keep redoing it perfectionism

entries.title: Stress & overload
entries.summary: Demands may exceed the time, energy or resources someone feels they have.

entries.title: Procrastination & making a start
entries.summary: Turn an intention into a feasible next action while checking resources, task feelings and obstacles.
entries.keywords: procrastination putting off delaying implementation intentions mental contrasting if then plans motivation studying task aversion

entries.title: Social comparison & envy
entries.summary: Understand comparison with other people without treating every comparison as harmful or every disappointment as envy.
entries.keywords: envy jealousy comparison upward downward social media success status resentment inferiority inspiration schadenfreude

entries.title: Shame, anger & taking responsibility
entries.summary: Distinguish a judgment about the whole self from concern about an action, without inferring emotions from outward conduct.
entries.keywords: shame guilt anger embarrassment humiliation defensive rage self worth blame repair emotion regulation

groups.title: Context, relationships & development
groups.description: Family, culture, life stages, resources and circumstances around an interaction.

entries.title: Adolescence: autonomy, peers & support
entries.summary: A young person’s wish for privacy or independence sits alongside learning, relationships, sleep, responsibilities and real constraints.

entries.title: Changing roles & life transitions
entries.summary: Moving, becoming a parent, changing work, retirement or taking on care can alter what people need from one another.

entries.title: Children: ability, learning & expectations
entries.summary: Before interpreting a child’s action as unwillingness, consider what they understand, can do and can manage in that setting.

entries.title: Culture & power
entries.summary: Consider the expectations, roles and unequal choices around an interaction.

entries.title: Culture: meanings without stereotypes
entries.summary: People can use different rules for respect, advice, privacy, duty and disagreement—even within the same family or community.

entries.title: Family expectations
entries.summary: Families differ in what they treat as ordinary involvement, duty, privacy and disagreement.

entries.title: Grief, loss & changing needs
entries.summary: Loss can change energy, attention, feelings and what kind of contact is welcome. It need not follow a fixed sequence or timetable.

entries.title: Language, accent & communication context
entries.summary: Fluency, speed, directness and pauses are imperfect guides to understanding, competence or honesty.

entries.title: Later life: change without age stereotypes
entries.summary: Age alone does not tell you someone’s competence, openness, motives or preferred amount of help.

entries.title: Low mood, withdrawal & support
entries.summary: Persistent low mood or loss of interest with difficulty in daily life deserves attention. Withdrawal alone does not establish depression.

entries.title: Neurodiversity & communication fit
entries.summary: People differ in how they process information, communicate and manage sensory demands. Ask about useful conditions without inferring a diagnosis.

entries.title: New changes in behaviour or functioning
entries.summary: A substantial change from someone’s usual behaviour can call for a health conversation rather than a personality explanation.

entries.title: Relationship history
entries.summary: Earlier agreements, disappointments or repairs can matter to a present interaction.

entries.title: Rules, exclusion & unequal access
entries.summary: A person’s options can be constrained by rules, costs, discrimination or inaccessible arrangements, rather than their motivation.

entries.title: Time, resources & capacity
entries.summary: Whether a person can carry out an action with the resources available.

entries.title: Trauma, reminders & present safety
entries.summary: Past frightening experiences can matter to current reactions, but a strong reaction does not reveal someone’s history.

entries.title: Unequal power
entries.summary: People differ in their ability to refuse, disagree or leave without serious consequences.

entries.title: Who else is present
entries.summary: The people watching an interaction may change its meaning or consequences.

entries.title: Worry, avoidance & reassurance
entries.summary: Worry can be a response to a real problem. Persistent fear or avoidance that restricts life may also call for professional support.

entries.title: Family membership, roles & loyalties
entries.summary: Understand uncertainty about who belongs, who has responsibilities and how family roles change.

entries.summary: Understand dimensions of relationship expectations without assigning fixed types or diagnoses.

entries.title: Access, participation & gatekeeping
entries.summary: Examine how someone facilitates or restricts participation while distinguishing privacy, care and safety duties.

entries.title: Children carrying adult responsibilities
entries.summary: Distinguish developmentally inappropriate adult roles from supported, age-appropriate family contribution.

entries.title: Messages, tone & delayed replies
entries.summary: Interpret short or unanswered messages with attention to wording, medium, expectations and missing information.

groups.title: Responding & collaborating
groups.description: Listen, make requests, agree responsibilities, repair and review.

entries.title: Boundaries
entries.summary: Decide what you will do when a behaviour affects you, without needing certainty about its motive.

entries.title: Compare explanations
entries.summary: Ask what would look different if another explanation were true.

entries.title: Getting support without needing a label
entries.summary: You can seek help for distress, changes in functioning or harmful treatment before knowing their cause.

entries.title: Make a clear request
entries.summary: Specify the action, timing and scope of what you are asking, while allowing an answer.

entries.title: Make a workable agreement
entries.summary: Specify responsibilities, constraints, timing and how either person can raise a problem.

entries.title: Notice what helps
entries.summary: Describe a helpful action and its effect so that good experiences can be understood and remembered.

entries.title: Reciprocity & mutual consideration
entries.summary: Making room for each person’s needs and contributions over time, without requiring every exchange to be identical.
entries.keywords: reciprocity mutual respect give and take one sided relationship healthy relationship

entries.title: Review what happened
entries.summary: Return to the outcome of an action and revise your explanation where appropriate.

entries.title: Support someone’s next step
entries.summary: Ask what support would help and offer a manageable contribution while preserving choice.

entries.title: Taking responsibility & making corrections
entries.summary: Acknowledging one’s specific actions and their consequences, correcting errors and making realistic changes.
entries.keywords: accountability they own their mistakes taking responsibility admitting mistakes

entries.title: Support that feels helpful
entries.summary: Match help to the person’s concern, choices and capabilities, and check whether it helped.

entries.title: Oversight, delegation & micromanagement
entries.summary: Distinguish proportionate checks from unnecessary control and agree ownership of shared work.
entries.keywords: micromanaging micromanagement delegation oversight supervision manager checking trust autonomy decision rights accountability

entries.title: Feedback & speaking up
entries.summary: Give task-focused feedback and examine whether people can raise a concern without costly consequences.
entries.keywords: feedback psychological safety speak up criticism manager coaching errors mistakes dissent retaliation voice sandwich

entries.title: Use AI without reinforcing a first impression
entries.summary: Use an LLM to organise questions and alternatives while keeping generated suggestions separate from observations.

entries.title: Negotiate a workable difference
entries.summary: Compare interests, options and alternatives while recognising limits to bargaining and mediation.

groups.title: Clinical vocabulary & support
groups.description: Understand terminology and distinctions without diagnosing yourself or another person.

entries.title: Antisocial personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving a pervasive disregard for others’ rights and consequences, assessed with the person’s developmental history and broader behaviour.
entries.keywords: antisocial personality disorder aspd sociopath psychopath

entries.title: Avoidant personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving pervasive social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy and sensitivity to negative evaluation, with significant effects on life.
entries.keywords: avoidant personality disorder avpd

entries.title: Borderline personality disorder (BPD)
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving persistent difficulties with emotional regulation, self-image, relationships and often impulsivity; assessment considers the full pattern and impact.
entries.keywords: borderline personality disorder borderline bpd

entries.title: Dependent personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving a pervasive, excessive need to be cared for, associated with difficulty acting independently and fear of separation.
entries.keywords: dependent personality disorder dpd

entries.title: Histrionic personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving a pervasive pattern of excessive emotional expression and attention-seeking, assessed in context and in relation to functioning.
entries.keywords: histrionic personality disorder hpd

entries.title: Narcissistic personality disorder (NPD)
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving a pervasive pattern of grandiosity, need for admiration and difficulties with empathy, assessed in the context of functioning and history.
entries.keywords: narcissistic personality disorder npd narcissist

entries.title: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
entries.summary: A condition involving recurring obsessions, compulsions or both, often taking time, causing distress or interfering with daily life.
entries.keywords: obsessive compulsive disorder ocd

entries.title: Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD)
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving a pervasive preoccupation with order, perfectionism and control that reduces flexibility or interferes with functioning.
entries.keywords: obsessive compulsive personality disorder ocpd

entries.title: Paranoid personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving pervasive, unwarranted distrust and suspicion, including interpreting others’ motives as hostile or harmful.
entries.keywords: paranoid personality disorder ppd

entries.title: Personality disorders: what the term means
entries.summary: Clinical terms for enduring, pervasive difficulties in patterns of thinking, feeling, relating or responding, associated with significant distress or problems functioning.
entries.keywords: personality disorder personality disorders pd

entries.title: Schizoid personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving pervasive detachment from social relationships and limited outward emotional expression, assessed within the broader pattern of functioning.
entries.keywords: schizoid personality disorder schizoid

entries.title: Schizotypal personality disorder
entries.summary: A clinical condition involving persistent difficulties with close relationships alongside unusual thinking, perceptions or behaviour, requiring assessment of the wider context.
entries.keywords: schizotypal personality disorder schizotypal stpd
